span.label: how quickly the auditory spatial map is recalibrated by conflicting visual information, and whether accumulated evidence of error is required to trigger it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: is cross-sensory recalibration engaged from the first discrepancy, or only after repeated and consistent error

span.label: shows the auditory spatial map shifts after a single 35 ms exposure to an audiovisual discrepancy, so recalibration is continuously operational rather than triggered by accumulated error

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Vision acts as a teaching signal that corrects the auditory spatial map because visual location estimates are far more reliable (lower response variance) than auditory ones, producing self-supervised learning without external feedback
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Perceived unity of the two signals plus the size of the discrepancy jointly gate recalibration, so a sizable map shift happens only when the conflict is likely to reflect systematic error rather than noise, which keeps the perceptual system stable
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the field's default position is diagnosed as an artefact of which experiments existed: no one had tested single exposures, so the accumulation account won implicitly
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the experiment is not built but found - pseudorandom interleaving in a dataset collected for another question makes every auditory trial's predecessor a single-exposure manipulation
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: two accounts that agree on most trials are separated by isolating the subset where they predict opposite directions
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the dependent measure is defined relative to each observer's own average response to that sound position, so a shift of zero is what randomness would give
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the preceding-auditory-trial condition serves as the control that a general response bias would also have produced, and it shows nothing

span.label: the stability objection is answered by the unity dependence: large shifts happen only when the signals are taken to share a source, which is when a discrepancy implies a real error
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A response-level (rather than perceptual) account of the visual bias cannot be ruled out.
span.note: what this limits: the perceptual interpretation of the visual bias: a response-level account CANNOT BE RULED OUT, though previous sound position had no effect on the current auditory response
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The reason the effect fails to cross the midline is undetermined.
span.note: what this limits: the hemifield result specifically: IT IS NOT CLEAR WHETHER THIS REFLECTS A MIDLINE BOUNDARY or something else - the effect does not transfer across hemifields
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Perceived unity was inferred from spatial judgements rather than reported by observers.
span.note: what this limits: any claim resting on perceived unity: it was inferred from spatial judgements rather than reported by the observers
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The trajectory of recalibration over repeated exposures needs a dedicated, larger and blocked design.
span.note: what this limits: the time course of recalibration: FUTURE STUDIES SHOULD FURTHER EXPLORE THE DYNAMICS OF RECALIBRATION ... WITH LARGER SAMPLE SIZES AND ADDITIONAL NUMBER OF REPETITIONS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the visual-location bias cannot be shown to be perceptual rather than a decision-level response bias
span.note: what this limits: the perceptual interpretation of the visual-location bias: a general response bias explanation is LESS LIKELY; HOWEVER, THIS EXPLANATION CANNOT BE RULED OUT
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: why vision teaches audition and not the reverse is undecided between reliability weighting and a fixed teacher role

Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the randomly varying discrepancies may themselves have induced an unusually plastic state
span.note: what this limits: the recalibration rate reported here: EXPOSURE TO RANDOMLY VARYING DISCREPANCIES ACROSS TRIALS IN THIS EXPERIMENT INDUCED THE NERVOUS SYSTEM TO ENTER A 'PLASTIC STATE', THUS RESULTING [in] A HIGHER RATE OF RECALIBRATION THAN USUAL
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: whether the shift is capped or the learning rate slows is not resolved
span.note: what this limits: the plateau in the shift: it COULD BE DUE TO A HARDWIRED CAP ON THE DEGREE OF CHANGE IN THESE BASIC MAPS, OR ALTERNATIVELY, DUE TO A SLOWING DOWN OF THE LEARNING RATE

span.label: perception → learning
span.note: NO BOUNDARY CAN BE DRAWN - the CONCEPTUAL form of the negative relation (Q-286/Q-287). This is a claim about the concepts themselves, not about this study's data. No edge type can express it: all eight assert that a relation HOLDS. Four words that dissolve a boundary two literatures are built on. There is nowhere in the schema for a FINDING WHOSE CONTENT IS THAT A DISTINCTION IS LESS SHARP THAN ASSUMED.

span.label: A single 35 ms exposure to a spatially discrepant sound-and-flash pair shifted where the next isolated sound was heard, showing that auditory spatial recalibration needs no prolonged exposure.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The shift followed the sign and size of the audio-visual discrepancy rather than the absolute position of the seen stimulus, identifying it as recalibration of the auditory map rather than a bias toward the visual location.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Separately from recalibration, auditory localisation was pulled toward the absolute position of the visual stimulus presented on the preceding unisensory visual trial.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The position of a preceding unisensory auditory stimulus had no significant effect on the current auditory judgement, arguing against a simple response bias.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Recalibration was much stronger after audio-visual trials where the two signals were judged to come from one source, so perceived unity gates the size of the shift.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Repeating discrepancies in the same direction accumulated a progressively larger shift, but at a decelerating rate, implying a decreasing learning rate rather than a fixed step.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The recalibration was one-directional: no corresponding shift of the visual spatial map by sound was detectable.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The effect weakened the further back in the trial history the audio-visual exposure lay, because intervening discrepancies pushed in other directions.
